title: The readout, turned
direction: A×C · Round 9 · /reports · document sheets (kit §12.5, .ac-sheet--spread) turned by the kit's segmented control (§5 .ac-seg), on the paper surface
summary: The same document as the head plate, set once and shown a spread at a time: the kit's segmented control (an ARIA tablist: 1 Narrative readout · 2 Channel orchestration map · 3 Intelligence gap report · 4 Sequenced rebuild plan) cuts between four spreads in one stage, each with the part and what was found on the verso (citing its exhibit) and one exhibit on the recto (four voices, a two-column channel ledger with the unrecorded channels shaded, a decision table, the plan as numbered steps), written for the invented company named on page 1; “Specimen” said once, in the label row.
story: The proof beat, answered honestly and at reading scale: not a client's readout but the document itself, in the voice a client receives, one spread per view. The visitor leafs through it with one real control instead of scrolling past four stacked boxes. Nothing in it is a result: the findings are diagnoses (who says what, where a touch is recorded, what a decision rested on, what to do first), drawn only from what the audit's stated scope shows (two working sessions, read-only CRM and channel stack).

reference.site: printed consulting readouts (verso/recto running heads, folios, exhibits cited in the text) · document viewers (one spread at a time, a contents strip as the control) · GoNimbly (few, large, sentence-case words per view)
reference.borrowed: A report spread: the chapter's text on the left, its exhibit on the right, the exhibit cited in the text; a viewer that turns one spread at a time.
reference.kelwin: The kit's sheet on the paper surface's --panel desk, turned by the kit's own segmented control (no new control). Column heads in the key voice; mono only for the folios (2 per view). Retired from round 9a: four stacked spreads (3,617px at 1440, 6,314px at 390), per-row keys on narrow pages, “Specimen” ×5, uncited exhibit numbers.

motion: entrance (once, when the slot plays): the control row and “Specimen” fade in; the spread rises (kit ac-up, 700ms).

interaction: the segmented control is an ARIA tablist (roving tabindex; ← → ↑ ↓ Home End move and select). Switching is a hard cut — the panel's hidden flag flips, nothing animates. Below 1024 one quiet “Next: <part>” (.ac-go--to) under the spread selects the next part and brings the control back into view.

on the live site: the same (init(root) returns a cleanup that restores part 1 and removes its listeners). Without script (@media (scripting: none)) the control hides and every spread is shown, stacked.
reduced motion: no entrance; the control works the same (it never animated).

phone: The control and the exhibits answer the room they have (container queries), not the viewport: the control is one row while its four parts fit (≥1,080px), two by two below, one column under 560px; on a page whose body is under 400px a table row's name sits above its values and a column head that would repeat is shown once (Exhibit 2: the caption names the column; Exhibit 3: “Based on | Missing” once over two columns). A spread keeps 2 : 1.414 as a minimum (100cqw × .707) and grows when its pages need more, so nothing is clipped at 1024–1439 (measured at 1024, 1100, 1280, 1366: every folio inside its page, no body overflow). ≤1023: full measure, the quiet “Next” under the spread. ≤767: each spread is two pages, one under the other (kit). Checked at 1440 (stitched), 1366, 1280, 1100, 1024, 834, 390, 320 (qa/r9-pages/reports/tab-*.png, look-*.png).
notes: Four parts confirmed (Q3). Rule 7: “Specimen” once for the whole document in the label row (page 1 says it on the plate); the invented company is named on page 1. No client, no figure that reads as a result, no chips, leaders, brackets or greeking; mono only for the two folios per view. Exhibits are numbered and every one is cited in the text. The time words inside the specimen are the invented company's facts (“within the hour”, “the last two quarters”, “each month”, “a quarter of closed deals”), never an engagement length. Visible words per view at 1440: 127–154 including the control (15), label, “Specimen” and running heads; the spreads' own text 95–122 (round 9a: 727 in the section). Paper surface because the object is a paper document (plan §7.5). The section is ≈1,160px tall at 1440 (round 9a: 3,617px).
